supports_model.mismatch_notes: The source equations are supported exactly: Lee Eqs. (20) and (26)-(32), PDF pp.6-8, as implemented in raosim/mdo/pump.py, raosim/mdo/engine.py and raosim/pumps.py (motor density on shaft output; inverter density on output = shaft/eta_m; battery power and energy branches with kappa_b; eta_E = eta_discharge). Support stays PARTIAL, as the 2026-10-14 review recorded: per-stream drives, the default technology set and its efficiencies and densities (repository_screening_v1 lies outside held evidence; P2 gap G4), bus selection and the electrical/thermal screens are repository extensions. The NLP objective uses a log-sum-exp upper envelope of Eq. (32); installed mass uses the exact MAX.

model_review.citation_vs_support: The equation reference 'Lee PDF pp. 6-8, Eqs. (20), (26)-(32)' is accurate (page-verified). The registry relation also covers technology-specific inputs, whose default values are repository choices outside the held sources (P2).
model_review.software_verification: Not re-run here; registry lists power/energy identity and Lee reference-point tests.
model_review.physical_validation: NOT_ESTABLISHED: Lee states no additional validation of component mass estimates (PDF p.10).
model_review.sensitivity: Not assessed (the P2 record notes the electric package dominates the MDO objective).
model_review.physics_finding: Sizing relations agree with Lee. Remaining issues are inputs (technology-set values and basis; see P2) and the pump-mass method, not the drive equations.
remaining_uncertainties: technology-set values (inverter 15 kW/kg and 0.96 efficiency in repository_screening_v1 lie outside held sources; P2)
eta_E is not tied to burn time as in Lee Eq. (38)
no thermal or pulse derating of motor or battery
